proposals.hypothesis: Li3TaO4 is the Ta5+ analogue of Li3NbO4, the best coating so far. It keeps the Li-rich, basic, d0 Group-5 oxide chemistry that resists reduction, and Ta is typically less reducible than Nb, which may weaken the Co/Al/Cl and P/S contact channels. It should also remain a wide-gap insulator.
proposals.motivation: Li3NbO4 (mp-aaaabupc) was insulating with band gap 5.56 eV, zero self-decomposition, and the lowest contact penalty so far (0.096 eV, bin 4). LiTaO3 gave a worse penalty (0.337), so the Li-richness may matter more than the metal swap alone.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV) electronic insulator with good chemical compatibility toward both the sulfide electrolyte and the oxide cathode, and it is a well-known Li-conducting coating. Its phosphate chemistry should limit reactions with Li6PS5Cl and LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and it does not add an electronically conductive path.

LiF is a very wide-gap ionic insulator with no reducible cation, so it should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl and oxidation at the 4.0 V LiCoO2 interface. Fluoride chemistry is also a common, chemically stable coating motif, and it is a different family from the phosphate tried so far, which gave a penalty of 0.337 eV.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with band gap 5.7 eV but had a contact penalty of 0.337 eV from decomposition toward P2O5/SCl4/SO2, which is well above the 0.05 eV target. Exploring a fluoride family may avoid that sulfur/phosphorus oxidation channel.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap Li-rich oxide whose Zr4+ cation is very hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte. Its Li-rich, sulfur-free chemistry avoids the P2O5/SO2/SCl4 oxidation channel that gave penalties of about 0.31 to 0.34 eV for Li3PO4 and LiF. It is also a known stable coating motif for LiCoO2 at 4 V.
proposal.motivation: Both Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs, penalty 0.310) and LiF (mp-aaaaabru, penalty 0.337) were insulating with wide gaps but decomposed toward P/S/Cl oxidation products at the sulfide contact. A Zr-based Li-rich oxide targets a different reaction channel and should be less oxidizing toward the sulfide.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlCl4 is a chloride with a hard-to-reduce Al3+ cation and a chloride anion that is compatible with the Cl-bearing sulfide electrolyte. Earlier oxide and fluoride coatings (Li3PO4, LiF, Li2ZrO3) all gave penalties of about 0.31 to 0.34 eV from P/S/SO2 oxidation channels at the sulfide contact. A chloride chemistry may avoid those channels and is a different family from all tested so far.
